confirmed.element: .record / .record-tag inside .plot, and @keyframes draw
confirmed.problem: `.record` is a zero-height element (`height: 0`, `border-top: 1px dashed`) carrying `animation: draw ... both`, whose `to` frame sets `clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0)`. A clip-path clips to the element's own border box — here 686×1px — and `.record-tag` is positioned at `top: -18px`, entirely outside it. Measured on the real file at 1440: `.record` computes `clip-path: inset(0px 0% 0px 0px)`, the tag's box is 103×15 at y 433 while the record box is 1px tall at y 450, and a pixel clip of the tag's own rectangle is a blank 206-byte PNG as built versus 1055 bytes with the clip forced off. This holds in settled, in `?motion=play`, on the dark ground, and under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` — the media query's `.record { clip-path: none }` is a normal declaration and is outranked by the animation's filled value, so the author's own escape hatch does not fire. 'Best week · 8' has never rendered, at any width, in any state.
confirmed.consequence: The chart draws a dashed horizontal line across it with no legend anywhere on the visible surface. The reader has to invent a meaning for it, and the obvious guesses — an average, a target — are not what it is. The line is the only thing on the screen that answers 'is this stretch better or worse than my normal', which is half the brief, and sighted readers never get told what it marks. Only the screen-reader sentence carries the fact.
confirmed.fix: Two edits, no reserved gutter. (1) In chart(), emit the tag as a SIBLING of .record inside .plot and give it its own --r: `Best week · ${D.bestPrior}` — the inline --r must be repeated, it is not inherited from a sibling. (2) Replace the .record-tag rule with `position: absolute; left: 0; right: auto; bottom: calc(var(--r) * 1%); margin-bottom: 4px; color: var(--ink-3); background: var(--paper); padding-right: var(--gap-hair);`. Left, not right: the record sits at 8 and every historical column tops out at 7 or below, so the left end of the rule is clear paper while the right end is permanently under the twelfth column, which is the hatched partial bucket and a protected object that must not be knocked out by the label's paper background. Measured with this applied at 390/768/1280/1440: the tag hit-tests as itself at all ten sample points across its width, overlaps zero bars at every breakpoint, column width is unchanged (22 / 43.5 / 53.5 / 53.5), and the x-axis sync is unchanged from baseline. Do NOT add padding-right to .record or .gridline — it is provably inert on a zero-height left:0/right:0 box — and do NOT add it to .cols. One sub-claim does not reproduce here: I sampled the rail region at 4x for any pixel with saturation > 0.12 and found zero, so on this Windows build U+2611 resolves to a monochrome Segoe UI Symbol, not an emoji face. The seat hedged that as conditional, so it is not an error, but it is not evidence either. WHAT FAILS IS THE FIX. "Inline SVG paths at 13px ... on the same 12x12 grid as ICON" is self-contradictory and mis-sized. ICON's marks are authored `<svg width="12" height="12" viewBox="0 0 12 12">`, so they render at 12px and the "13px" is either ignored or, if forced, scales a 12-unit grid by 1.0833 and lands ICON's 1.5-1.6 strokes at 1.625 device px off the pixel grid at 1x - blurring hairlines on a surface whose entire icon system is deliberately integer-snapped. Worse, 12x12 is the wrong grid for this tile regardless of the scaling: .glyph chips are 20x20 carrying 12px marks (ratio 0.60), while .rail i is 26x26 (measured 26x26 at 1440). A 12px mark in a 26px tile is ratio 0.46 - the four rail marks would land visibly smaller and lighter than every other chip on the surface, and lighter than the fallback glyphs they replace, which optically fill ~14-15px today. The fix direction is right; its two numbers are both wrong.
confirmed.sharpenedFix: Keep the direction - replace the four characters in shell()'s .rail markup with inline SVG in currentColor, aria-hidden, authored in ICON's stroke language - but fix the geometry. Draw on a 16x16 grid rendered at exactly 16px (`<svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16">`), integer 1:1, which holds the 0.60 mark-to-tile ratio the 20px .glyph chips already establish (16/26 = 0.62). Hold stroke-width at 1.5 with stroke-linecap/linejoin round, identical to ICON.still/past/nobody/waiting, so the rail reads as the same pen rather than a scaled-up copy. Use `stroke="currentColor"` only - never ICON's hard-coded status hexes, which are reserved for the four status meanings and would import amber/red/indigo/emerald into inert furniture. currentColor is required, not optional, because .rail i.on inverts to color:var(--paper) on background:var(--ink).
